claims.text: What the image looks like Buzzword: onion-skin periostitis on bone X-ray → Ewing sarcoma
claims.quote: Onion-skin periostitis Bone X-ray Ewing sarcoma

claims.text: Lytic destruction, particularly a permeative pattern, is the most common finding on imaging, but multiple layers of subperiosteal reactive new bone formation may give an onion-skin appearance
claims.quote: Lytic destruction, particularly a permeative pattern, is the most common finding on imaging, but multiple layers of subperiosteal reactive new bone formation may give an onion-skin appearance.

claims.text: Radiographs classically do not usually reveal the full extent of bone involvement, and a large soft tissue mass usually surrounds the affected bone; MRI better defines disease extent, which can help guide treatment
claims.quote: Radiographs classically do not usually reveal the full extent of bone involvement, and a large soft tissue mass usually surrounds the affected bone. MRI better defines disease extent, which can help guide treatment.

claims.text: Example radial-shaft radiograph: subperiosteal reactive new bone formation in a classic "sunburst" periosteal reaction along with lytic destruction of cortical bone
claims.quote: This Ewing sarcoma of the radial shaft shows subperiosteal reactive new bone formation in a classic "sunburst" periosteal reaction along with lytic destruction of cortical bone.
claims.locator: Ewing Sarcoma of the Radius image caption

claims.text: Example shoulder radiograph: a permeative destructive tumor arising in the proximal humerus, typical of Ewing sarcoma
claims.quote: This shoulder radiograph shows a permeative destructive tumor arising in the proximal humerus, which is typical of Ewing sarcoma.
claims.locator: Ewing Sarcoma of Bone image caption

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) Site: most tumors develop in the extremities, but any bone may be involved; most often the diaphyseal region, with some extension into the metaphyseal region
claims.quote: Most tumors develop in the extremities, but any bone may be involved. Ewing sarcoma most often involves the diaphyseal region with some extension into the metaphyseal region.

claims.text: Many other benign and malignant tumors can appear very similarly, so diagnosis is made by biopsy; at times this tumor may be confused with an infection
claims.quote: Many other benign and malignant tumors can appear very similarly, so diagnosis of Ewing sarcoma is made by biopsy. At times this type of tumor may be confused with an infection.

claims.text: Causes Small blue round-cell bone tumor with a peak incidence between 10 and 20 years; related to peripheral primitive neuroectodermal tumors (PNET) and Askin malignant small cell tumor of the chest wall, now considered part of the Ewing sarcoma family of tumors
claims.quote: Ewing sarcoma of bone is a small blue round-cell bone tumor with a peak incidence between 10 and 20 years. Ewing sarcoma is related to peripheral primitive neuroectodermal tumors (PNET) and Askin malignant small cell tumor of the chest wall, which are now considered part of the Ewing sarcoma family of tumors.

claims.text: Molecular marker: a typical translocation between chromosomes 11 and 22 resulting in the EWSR1-FLI1 fusion product, present in approximately 85% of cases (several other translocations have been identified)
claims.quote: identification of molecular markers, including evaluation for a typical chromosomal translocation between chromosomes 11 and 22 resulting in the EWSR1-FLI1 fusion product. This fusion product is present in approximately 85% of cases; however, several different structural translocations in different fusion gene patterns have been identified

claims.text: Symptoms Pain and swelling are the most common symptoms
claims.quote: Pain and swelling are the most common symptoms.

claims.text: Treatment and next step Chemotherapy and surgery with or without radiation therapy; currently > 60% of patients with primary localized Ewing sarcoma may be cured by this multimodal approach, and cure is sometimes possible even with metastatic disease
claims.quote: Treatment of Ewing sarcoma includes chemotherapy and surgery with or without radiation therapy. Currently, > 60% of patients with primary localized Ewing sarcoma may be cured by this multimodal approach (7). Cure is sometimes possible even with metastatic disease.

claims.text: Chemotherapy with surgical en bloc resection, if possible, has a lower rate of local relapse than chemotherapy with radiation therapy (the differences are small and must be weighed against the morbidity of resection); most often, surgery is favored when possible
claims.quote: Chemotherapy in conjunction with surgical en bloc resection, if possible, has a lower rate of local relapse than chemotherapy in conjunction with radiation therapy, although these differences are small and must be weighed against the morbidity of surgical resection. Most often, surgery is favored when possible.
